rationale: The headline result reproduces cleanly. From outputs/table4.json (Table IV, 1970 Census, men born 1920-1929, n=247,199), the OLS return to education (col1) is 0.08016 and the TSLS return with EDUC instrumented by the 30 QOB-by-YOB interactions (col2) is 0.07686 with the overid dof (29) matching the design — essentially identical to the paper's Table IV col 2 = 0.0769. Against the claim's paper_value, the OLS return (0.0802 vs 0.08) is 0.2% relative error and the TSLS return (0.0769 vs 0.075) is 2.5% relative error, both inside the 5% match band, and the two estimates are 'hardly different' from each other (0.077 vs 0.080) exactly as claimed. The fix_severity.json records only a single 'major' fix — a faithful Stata-to-R language port (reg->lm, ivregress 2sls->AER::ivreg) driven by toolchain availability, with no methodological change (critical_count=0) — so the produced IV estimate faithfully reflects the paper's method.

Examples: YOB30 Q1=12.280 vs Q2-Q4 12.428/12.492/12.625; YOB40 Q1=13.019 vs 13.056/13.159/13.266; YOB46 Q1=13.617 vs 13.689/13.788/13.860. All examined cohorts (1930-1949) have RISING secular education; the declining-secular cohorts (1950-1959) are absent from the extract and could not be examined.
structured.claim_paraphrase: In virtually all birth cohorts, first-quarter-born men have slightly lower average completed education than men born later in the year, and this seasonal dip holds for cohorts with both rising and declining secular education levels.

rationale: The primary described behavior is unambiguously reproduced: in outputs/figures.json (fig1_2_mean_educ_by_yob_qob) the first-quarter mean education is the lowest or near-lowest quarter in virtually every examined birth year (e.g. YOB30 Q1=12.280 < 12.428/12.492/12.625; YOB40 Q1=13.019 < 13.056/13.159/13.266; YOB46 Q1=13.617 < 13.689/13.788/13.860), and the detrended series records the Q1 mean below the MA(+2,-2) prediction in 18 of 19 birth-years (fig4_q1_below_ma = {count:18,total:19}); the figure1_2_education.png visibly shows the black 'Q1' line sitting at the bottom of each year's cluster. Only YOB49 reverses the pattern (Q1 highest). This fully supports the 'Q1 has lower average education than later-quarter births across cohorts' portion of the claim. However, the claim also asserts the pattern holds 'for cohorts with both rising and declining secular education levels' and the paper_value references cohorts 1930-1959; the shipped NEW7080 extract spans only birth years 1930-1949 (all rising-secular cohorts), and the plan/step-7 log explicitly flag that the 1950-1959 declining-secular panels are NOT reproducible from this data (figures.json 'note'; step 7 notes 'LIMITATION ... 1950-1959 ... NOT reproducible'). Thus the rising-cohort half of the two-regime sub-claim is strongly confirmed while the declining-cohort half cannot be demonstrated (not contradicted, merely absent), making this a partial rather than full match. The only code change (fix_severity.json) is a Stata->R port rated 'major' with no methodological defect, so it does not undermine the produced cell means.

Step 6 reproduced Table I via the MA(+2,-2) detrended regression of years of education on quarter-of-birth dummies. In outputs/table1.json the 'total_education' blocks give the quarter-1 main effect (relative to quarter 4): for the 1930-1939 cohort est=-0.11941612 (se 0.01719015, n=294196, F=25.06) and for the 1940-1949 cohort est=-0.08441265 (se 0.01274599, n=438507, F=16.25). Both are negative and about one tenth of a year, matching the paper's claim. Compared to paper_value (-0.124, se 0.017; -0.085, se 0.012), the 1930s deviation is ~0.005 (<0.3σ) and the 1940s deviation is ~0.0006 (<0.05σ) — both well within ±1σ. The only recorded fix (fix_severity.json) is a benign Stata-to-R port of the IV pipeline rated 'major' for effort, with no critical defect and no impact on the Table I method; the evidence note flags the positive-earnings extract as an approximate sample, consistent with the tiny observed offsets. Verdict: match on both cohorts.

The run produced outputs/table1.json (via step 6, table1_qob_education.R), which regresses each MA(+2,-2)-detrended educational outcome on QTR1-3 dummies for the 1930-39 and 1940-49 cohorts, exactly the Table I design. Cell-by-cell comparison against the paper is a mixed picture: the Q1 effects and the total-education F-stat replicate very closely (e.g. total educ 1930-39 Q1 -0.119 vs -0.124 =3.7%, F 25.06 vs 24.9 =0.6%; total educ 1940-49 Q1 -0.084 vs -0.085 =0.7%; HS grad 1930-39 Q1 -0.019 vs -0.019 =1%; college 1940-49 Q1 -0.003 vs -0.003 =1.7%), but many cells fall in the 5-30% band (total educ 1940-49 Q2 22%, Q3 11%, F 13%; HS grad 1940-49 F 46 vs 54 =16%; college Q2 effects 16-27%) and the near-zero Q3 cells drift beyond 30% purely because the paper's target is tiny (total educ 1930-39 Q3 +0.001 vs -0.015; college 1930-39 Q3 0.005 vs 0.002; college F 6.58 vs 5.0 =32%). The evidence_summary and replication_log both flag the cause: the shipped extract is the 'positive-earnings sample,' which differs slightly from the paper's education-based Table I sample, so magnitudes are approximate (fix_severity.json rates the only fix as a benign Stata->R port with no methodology gap). All qualitative checks required by the verification instructions pass: Q1 is negative for years-of-education and high-school-graduate in both cohorts, and college effects are small. Not every cell is within 5% (so not a full match) and not every cell exceeds 30% (so not a no_match); this is a partial.

The reproduced Table I (codebase/outputs/table1.json) high-school-graduate blocks give the quarter-1 main effect coef_I = -0.01879164 (SE 0.0022) for the 1930-1939 cohort and coef_I = -0.01414143 (SE 0.00145) for the 1940-1949 cohort, i.e. Q1 births are 1.88 pp (paper 1.9) and 1.41 pp (paper 1.5) less likely to graduate high school. The cohort means (0.77114 for 1930s, 0.86582 for 1940s) imply dropout rates of 0.229 (~23%, paper 23%) and 0.134 (~14%, paper 14%). Dividing the graduation gap by the dropout rate gives 0.01879/0.229 = 0.082 and 0.01414/0.134 = 0.105, i.e. roughly 10 percent higher dropout, matching the paper's 'roughly 10 percent'. The 1930s gap (1.88 vs 1.9, 1% off) and relative-increase are within band; the 1940s gap (1.41 vs 1.5) is ~6% off, consistent with the file's note that the shipped positive-earnings extract differs slightly from the paper's education-based Table I sample so magnitudes are approximate. All signs, magnitudes, and the derived relative increase confirm the claim.

structured.observed_behavior: In the reproduced Table I (outputs/table1.json), the post-secondary outcomes show quarter-of-birth main effects roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the compulsory-schooling outcomes and lack the systematic negative-Q1 pattern. College graduate: coef_I=-0.0043/II=+0.0035/III=+0.0045 (1930s), -0.0031/+0.0051/-0.00002 (1940s). Master's degree: coef_I=-0.0006/II=+0.0023/III=-0.0001 with F_p=0.200 (1930s, insignificant), +0.0002/+0.0042/+0.0010 (1940s). Doctoral degree: coef_I=+0.0017 (positive) /II=+0.0026/III=+0.0005 (1930s), -0.0015/+0.0010/-0.0005 (1940s). By contrast total_education has coef_I=-0.119/-0.084 and HS graduate coef_I=-0.019/-0.014, both clearly negative in Q1 with F_p between 1e-10 and 1e-29. Post-secondary coefficients are near zero, Q1 is not consistently negative (doctoral 1930s is positive, master's ~0), matching the paper's 'no discernible pattern'.
structured.claim_paraphrase: The quarter-of-birth (seasonal) education pattern present for total years of schooling and high-school graduation is absent for post-secondary outcomes (college graduation, master's completion, doctoral completion) that are not constrained by compulsory schooling.

rationale: From /workspace/output/replication/codebase/outputs/table1.json, the compulsory-schooling outcomes reproduce the strong negative-Q1 seasonal pattern (total_education coef_I=-0.11941612 [1930s] and -0.08441265 [1940s]; high_school_graduate coef_I=-0.01879164 and -0.01414143), all with F prob-values from 3.35e-16 down to 1.23e-29. The post-secondary rows show the pattern is absent: college_graduate, masters_degree, and doctoral_degree QOB coefficients are all near zero (magnitudes ~0.00002-0.005) and lack a systematic negative Q1 — master's Q1 is essentially zero and its 1930s F-test is insignificant (F_p=0.20006089, matching the paper's noted P≈0.1599), while doctoral Q1 for the 1930s is even positive (+0.00171809). This unambiguously demonstrates the claimed falsification result: no discernible seasonal pattern for post-high-school outcomes. The only major fix flagged in fix_severity.json concerns the Table 4 Stata->R 2SLS port, not the Table I / step-6 code path, so it does not undermine this result.
